clue.text: Strongholds in castle I'd converted

indicators.note: something converted has been changed into a new form, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A castle has been turned into a set of fortresses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'converted' rearranges the letters of CASTLE and ID together.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a citadel is a fortress guarding a city, a stronghold.

clue.text: Sweet, some music a keyboardist produces!

indicators.note: only some of the letters of these words are used, a run sitting across the word boundaries

explanation.surface: A keyboard player produces some delightful music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' marks the letters running across musiC A KEyboardist.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a cake is a sweet treat, and in Britain a dessert is often called a sweet.

clue.text: Irregularly, stayed outside university for part of the week

indicators.note: the shuffled letters stay outside, wrapped around the single letter for university
done irregularly means not in the usual order, so the letters of stayed are mixed up

explanation.surface: Someone stayed away from college on and off for part of the week.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Irregularly' turns STAYED into TESDAY, and 'outside' puts that around U.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: one of the seven days, the one after Monday.

clue.text: Rescue last of fine offal placed in skip

indicators.note: these pieces are set inside the word for skip

parts.note: to skip is to hop along lightly, to dance

indicators.note: takes only the final letter of the word fine

parts.note: liver is a kind of offal, an organ meat

explanation.surface: Leftover fine offal gets tossed into a rubbish skip.
explanation.walkthrough: A British skip is a large rubbish container, which sells the surface; here it is the verb, DANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: deliverance is being saved or set free from danger.

clue.text: Socialists exist, ignored?

parts.note: socialists are the political left
to exist is to be

explanation.surface: A wry question about whether socialists still exist, or whether they are ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: something left alone, not interfered with, has been passed over or ignored.

clue.text: Employer's bum steers, every so often

indicators.note: only letters at regular intervals are taken, here the second, fourth, sixth and eighth

explanation.surface: An employer is handing out bad advice now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: A bum steer is slang for misleading advice; 'every so often' takes bUm StEeRs.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: one who uses or employs something, as a tool or service.

clue.text: A very good man — I rock!

parts.note: a saint, abbreviated ST
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: A boastful saint declares he is a great rocker.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: stone is the hard mineral matter of which rock is made.

clue.text: Boy is to attempt record collection

parts.note: Reg is a boy's name, short for Reginald
taken as written
to try is to attempt

explanation.surface: A boy tries to put together a collection of records.
explanation.walkthrough: 'record collection' suggests vinyl albums; it means a collection of official records.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a registry is a place where official records are kept.

clue.text: Boy, we hear, to go on a bender

indicators.note: says the word is judged by how it sounds when spoken

parts.note: Neil is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A boy sounds like he is about to go out drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: A bender is a drinking spree; here it is what bends, the knee.
explanation.definitionFit: Pun: to get down on bended knee is jokingly to go on a bender.

clue.text: Hair needing to be cut, perhaps, though hardly extending this far!

parts.note: fur is animal hair
hair that needs cutting is long

explanation.surface: Overgrown hair may need cutting, though it is hardly that lengthy.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is that this distance, an eighth of a mile, is far longer than any hair grows.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a furlong is a unit of distance, 220 yards, used in horse racing.

clue.text: New author's Muir, they say

indicators.note: a new version of these letters is a fresh arrangement of them

parts.note: taken as written, without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Gossip about a newly published writer named Muir.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: both phrases introduce hearsay, something people report without proof.

clue.text: They drop to deadly effect — in two ways

definitions.text: They drop to deadly effect — in two ways

parts.words: They drop to deadly effect — in two ways
parts.note: these aircraft both plunge steeply and release explosives

explanation.surface: Something that falls with lethal results, by two routes.
explanation.walkthrough: The two ways are diving down on a target and dropping bombs on it.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: these warplanes swoop steeply at a target and release their payload.

clue.text: Gave Irish footballer ring midweek?

parts.note: George Best was a famous Northern Irish footballer
a ring is round like the letter O
Wed, short for Wednesday, the middle day of the week

explanation.surface: A question whether a footballer gave a ring halfway through the week.
explanation.walkthrough: GEORGE BEST was a Manchester United star from Belfast.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to bestow is to give or present something, often as an honour.

clue.text: Bear's friend in bygone days with body of deer

indicators.note: the body is the middle, so only the inner letters of deer are kept

parts.note: of yore means in days long past

explanation.surface: A tale from olden times of a bear's companion with a deer's body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' joins the pieces, and the deer's inner letters come first.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the gloomy donkey is a companion of Winnie-the-Pooh, a bear.

clue.text: One swearing aloud, finding something on computer screen

indicators.note: the word is judged by how it sounds when spoken

parts.note: a curser is one who curses or swears

explanation.surface: Someone cursing loudly at what they see on their computer screen.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the blinking pointer marking position on a display.

clue.text: Bribe artist, and no singer

parts.note: a sop is something given to pacify or bribe
RA, Royal Academician, a member of the Royal Academy of Arts
taken as written

explanation.surface: A painter is bribed, but he is no singer.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a soprano is a singer with the highest voice range.

clue.text: Naval hero's grip on opponent

definitions.meaning: a wrestling hold applied from behind the neck

explanation.surface: An admiral grapples with an enemy.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: Britain's famous admiral, and a wrestling hold with arms under the opponent's.

clue.text: Hen parties I organised: one's held by apprentice

indicators.note: organised letters are set into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone arranged hen parties, a job given to the trainee.
explanation.walkthrough: A hen party is a British pre-wedding party for the bride; 'organised' rearranges HENPARTIES with I.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a post for learning a trade is what an apprentice occupies.

clue.text: A pudding sent back cold

indicators.note: something sent back goes the other way, so the word for pudding is read backwards

parts.note: a fool is a pudding of fruit puree and cream

explanation.surface: A dessert returned to the kitchen because it was cold.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone aloof is distant and unfriendly, as a cold person is.

clue.text: Son heads for Klosters in Switzerland and …?

definitions.text: Son heads for Klosters in Switzerland and …?

indicators.note: the first letters of the following words are taken

explanation.surface: A son sets off for a Swiss ski resort, and what does he do there?
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: what a son heading for Klosters does.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: going down the slopes at a Swiss resort is the obvious activity.

clue.text: Are these speakers barking?

parts.note: loudspeakers for bass are named after a dog's bark

explanation.surface: A puzzled question whether some talkers are mad.
explanation.walkthrough: Barking is British slang for mad, but here it is literal: making a dog's noise.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: bass loudspeakers, whose name echoes the sound a dog makes.

clue.text: Heap of dust finally placed in bag

indicators.note: the letter is set inside the word for bag

parts.note: a sack is a large bag

indicators.note: takes only the final letter of the word dust

explanation.surface: A pile of dust is finally put into a bag.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a stack is a pile, things heaped up.

clue.text: Pudding that's no good

definitions.meaning: a boiled dough or suet dessert

explanation.surface: A dessert that is not much good.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a boiled suet dessert, and slang for broken or useless.

clue.text: Oily bend in pipe, perhaps, with suction breaking

parts.note: a U-bend is a curved section of plumbing

indicators.note: the letters of suction break up into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: An oily U-bend in a pipe, with the suction failing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking' rearranges SUCTION into NCTIOUS, after U.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an unctuous manner is greasy and ingratiating; literally the word means oily.
